name: screen-frame
title: Screen frame
description: A frame that fills the visible screen: header and footer stay put, the middle scrolls, and it copes with address bars, notches and keyboards.
docs: header and footer render as header and footer landmarks and stay put; children is the middle, the one part that scrolls, and you put main there. scroll="body" (the default) makes the middle one scrolling area; scroll="none" makes it a row for ScreenFrame.Pane, each of which scrolls on its own (as is div, section, aside or nav). The frame is as tall as the dynamic viewport (h-dvh), so the browser bar never hides the footer; give it a height of your own (h-full, h-[34rem]) to fill a box. The safe-area insets are padding on the frame, and the browser reports them when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover. keyboardAware (on by default) lifts the footer above the on-screen keyboard, measured through the visual viewport and ignoring pinch zoom; keyboardInset replaces the measurement when you know the height. The body has its overscroll contained; bodyClassName, headerClassName and footerClassName reach each part.
